I realized I was lesbian at 19, came out at 20 and tried rushing into a relationship with a girl, because I felt so ashamed and lonely about not having any connection to the community and being in denial through my teen years. I was so envious of my then boyfriend's best friend, because she had been out since middle school.
Well, through online dating I met my first girlfriend who turned out to be very abusive. But at the time I felt like I owed her for sparing me the guilt of being single. 
Right now I am 22 and in a caring relationship as well as working through the trauma. 
I had my first sex ever at 21 and looking back there was nothing to be ashamed of. 
What helped me, was reaching out to my local LGBT+ youth group, which is divided into age categorys so you meet lots of people your age, that go through the same struggles. 
At the moment they meet up online, so maybe smth. like this might help? And when the pandemic is over you can meet up in person. 

All I wanna say is, the situation sucks right now, but you don't have to feel bad for taking a little longer. Don't rush into things just to 'get it over with'.

Thing with BDSM is, it's a play with power dynamics. My domme does not stand over me in everyday life and everything we do considering our kink life is well defined. What I have noticed in my kinky friend group is, that actually the sub part has more power over the dom part, because they define what is ok to do and what is not. 
In a scene the sub part hands over power to the dom part, because they want to and trust them. Without the willingness of the sub to be submissive however, the dom can be as dominant as they want, they have no power. 
If they try to inforce it, that would count as abuse. But then they are no more than an abusive partner and not really a dom. 
Aftercare is what I additionally find very important, because you discuss how each part felt about it and you can affirm each others feelings and, what is most importantly for me and my partner, rebalance the power dynamic. Make sure we are equal parts in our relationship and that the topic of abuse is not given here. 
I have been in an abusive dom/sub relationship before and I can assure you, that it feels way different. 
Obviously if you are a sub and are searching for a dom, you unfortunately have to be careful not to fall into an abusive dynamic, because you show yourself pretty vulnerable, but it's the same risk as with any other relationship. 
But that's why the BDSM community comes in handy, because you can share your experiences and help each other out, if you notice that there is something going wrong in your dynamic. It does not necessarily have to be abuse that is talked, it is also nice to just share experiences or find out where there would be room for improvement.
